Solution: Volume change = area × height change = 50 x 2 = 100 cm³

A rectangular prism tank is completely full of water. The tank has: height = 13 cm, width = 15 cm, depth = 20 cm. After some water is removed, the water level drops to 6 cm. How much water was removed from the tank? Put the answer without units.
Hints: The water drop forms a smaller rectangular prism, so we can calculate its volume using base area × height
Solution: Step 1: Find how much the water level dropped: 13 - 6 = 7 cm. Step 2: Find the base area of the tank: 15 x 20 = 300 cm^2. Step 3: Find the volume of water removed: 300 x 7 = 2100 cm^3

Solution: Volume changes the same way, it doubles 2 times = 40 x 2 x 2 = 160
